steps: 4 insulated conductor allowances + 1 grounding allowances + 0 clamp allowance + 2 device-yoke allowances + 0 support allowance + 0 terminal-block assembly allowance(s) = 7.

Grounds: first 1–4 = one allowance; each additional = ¼ allowance. Each terminal-block assembly adds one allowance based on the largest conductor terminated; this uniform-size model uses the selected conductor size.
warnings: Named modeled NEC provisions were checked against published NEC 2023 on 2026-10-13. This is a bounded calculation aid, not certification of code compliance. Equipment listings, installation conditions, unmodeled exceptions, the locally adopted edition, amendments and AHJ requirements still need project-specific review.
NEC 2023 314.16(B)(1)–(6) and Table 314.16(B)(1). Uniform conductor size only. Count conductors entering and terminating or passing through; pigtails wholly within the box normally do not count.

Each standard device yoke counts as two allowances. One or more internal clamps count once; each support fitting type (stud or hickey) counts once, up to two allowances. Ground allowance assumes entering EGCs/bonding jumpers of the selected size. Every terminal-block assembly must be counted, and the selected uniform conductor size must include its largest terminated conductor.

Mixed sizes, long unbroken loops, larger/multiple-gang devices, barriers, luminaire exceptions and conductors larger than #6 require a separate review. Use the marked usable box/extension volume; do not infer volume from outside dimensions.
